title: Composition of derived direct images
statement: Let $X\xrightarrow{p}Y\xrightarrow{f}Z$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. On the derived categories of modules [def-pc-derived-direct-image], there is a canonical natural isomorphism $R(f\circ p)_*\cong Rf_*\circ Rp_*:D(\mathcal O_X)\to D(\mathcal O_Z)$.

proof.text: By [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-adjoint], $Lf^*$ is left adjoint to $Rf_*$ and $Lp^*$ is left adjoint to $Rp_*$. By [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-pullback-composition], there is a canonical natural isomorphism $Lp^*\circ Lf^*\cong L(f\circ p)^*$ (with the order understood as pullback first along $f$ and then along $p$). Transporting the adjunction $L(f\circ p)^*\dashv R(f\circ p)_*$ along this isomorphism makes $R(f\circ p)_*$ a right adjoint of $Lp^*\circ Lf^*$. The pasted adjunction from the two individual adjunctions has right adjoint $Rf_*\circ Rp_*$ by [lem-cat-right-adjoint-composition]. Uniqueness of right adjoints therefore gives the canonical natural isomorphism $R(f\circ p)_*\cong Rf_*\circ Rp_*$. This argument uses no properness or Noetherian hypothesis, so it applies under the hypotheses of the item.

proof.text: The identity and associativity laws for the direct-image comparison are the mates of the corresponding identity and associativity laws for derived pullback composition in [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-pullback-composition]. The pasted units and counits in [lem-cat-right-adjoint-composition] characterize these mates, and uniqueness of right adjoints preserves the coherence equations. Hence the canonical isomorphism is natural and has the stated canonical composition meaning.
